The 2026-05-10 recording was contaminated: hgemm/igemm were re-measured 2026-05-22 (median of 7 valid samples each, driver 595.97 / CUDA 13.2) and corrected — igemm_sparse_tiled 2048³ is 17% above (old recorded low). THREE configs now have no fair native-boost baseline and carry clock_lock: 1605 — igemm_sparse_tiled 4096³ (power-bound: draws >150 W, SwPowerCap throttles a varying fraction of the bench's 50 averaged launches) and BOTH hgemm_16warp configs (boost-unstable: the 2026-06-05 grid re-measured their native medians at 0.884 and 0.898 of their own 2026-05-22 native baselines, 5 of 7 samples below the 0.90 floor in each case, with throttle 'none' throughout — see #156 and the unexplained higher-clock-is-slower anomaly in #158). All three are SKIPPED by the native pre-push gate and measured only under bench_regress.R --clock-locked 1605. The remaining native-gated configs are igemm_sparse_tiled 2048³, igemm_pipelined_cpasync 4096³, flash_attn_br16_regpv 1024_8_8 and conv2d_implicit_gemm. Clock-lock IS available via the Windows-host nvidia-smi.exe (#125 verdict corrected).

default_valid_when.comment: Inherited by every kernel that doesn't set its own valid_when. Override per-kernel for stricter requirements (min_clock_sm, max_temp_c, require_ac).

schema.exe: (optional) path to bench binary; defaults to <kernel-dir>/bench or <kernel-dir>/bench_<basename>
schema.match: (optional) substring of the bench-output line that holds this kernel's number; required when bench.cu prints multiple kernels
schema.section: (optional) substring of a section header; parser only considers lines after this header until the next header
schema.value_label: (optional) text immediately following the throughput number on the matched line; required when the line has multiple numbers
schema.valid_when: (optional) GPU/host state requirement for a fair comparison; refuses to compare if violated. Fields: require_no_throttle (default TRUE), allow_throttle (default ['GpuIdle']), min_clock_sm (MHz), max_temp_c (degC), require_ac (laptop). Tier 10.
schema.tolerance: (optional) per-config tolerance override (fraction). Default is the CLI --tolerance (0.10). Use for kernels that are intrinsically noisy on this hardware.
schema.clock_lock: (optional) integer MHz. Marks a config that has NO REPRODUCIBLE NATIVE-BOOST BASELINE and is therefore only fair under a host-side SM clock lock (Windows: nvidia-smi.exe -lgc MHz,MHz, elevated). Two distinct mechanisms qualify: (a) power-bound — the kernel draws >150 W mid-run and a varying fraction of the bench's averaged launches hits SwPowerCap (igemm_sparse_tiled 4096); (b) boost-unstable — native-boost throughput is not reproducible run-to-run even though no throttle bit is ever observed (hgemm_16warp, #156/#158). The test for membership is empirical, not thermodynamic: if the config's native median sits below the regression floor of its own recorded native baseline, it has no fair native baseline. bench_regress.R SKIPs such a config unless invoked with --clock-locked <MHz> matching this value; when measured it collects a median of CLOCK_LOCK_SAMPLES valid runs and rejects any sample whose observed SM clock leaves the locked band. All locked configs share one lock point (1605 MHz) so a single elevated session gates them all. See docs/benchmark_methodology.md and issues #131, #156.

2048_2048_2048.note: No reproducible native-boost baseline (#156). Measured under a host-side clock lock (Windows nvidia-smi.exe -lgc 1605,1605, elevated): median of 7 valid samples, 2026-06-05, run grid-20260605-150125 @ 35c5057, driver 595.97, warmup 20, band ±30 MHz, spread 29033-29217 (1.006x), every sample observed at exactly 1605 MHz, throttle 'none'. Supersedes the native entry 0.540 / 31789 (2026-05-22, recorded at 1740-1770 MHz boost): the 2026-06-05 grid re-measured this config at native boost as median 28090 with 5 of 7 samples BELOW the 0.90 regression floor of that baseline (ratio 0.884, min 0.853) — the old number is a best-case boost window this laptop cannot reproduce, so it generated false REGRESSIONs on unrelated pushes. The locked number is lower than the old native record because the 1605 lock trades peak clock for reproducibility; at a 1710 lock this config measures 30842. Gated only when bench_regress.R is run with --clock-locked 1605; SKIPPED otherwise.

4096_4096_4096.note: No reproducible native-boost baseline (#156). Measured under a host-side clock lock (Windows nvidia-smi.exe -lgc 1605,1605, elevated): median of 7 valid samples, 2026-06-05, run grid-20260605-150125 @ 35c5057, driver 595.97, warmup 20, band ±30 MHz, spread 30205-30443 (1.008x), every sample observed at exactly 1605 MHz, throttle 'none'. Supersedes the native entry 4.521 / 30397 (2026-05-22, recorded at 1770-1785 MHz boost) — which the locked median reproduces to within 0.01%, so this is a provenance correction, not a number change. The same 2026-06-05 grid re-measured this config at native boost as median 27307 with 5 of 7 samples BELOW the 0.90 regression floor (ratio 0.898, min 0.888). ANOMALY (unexplained, see #158): at native the observed SM clock is HIGHER (1770-1785) and power HIGHER (median 118 W) yet throughput is 10% LOWER than at the 1605 lock (median 101 W), with throttle 'none' on every sample in both regimes — so this is not the >150 W SwPowerCap mechanism that gates igemm_sparse_tiled 4096. CROSS-SESSION DELTA (see #159): the 2026-06-03 #143 elevated session read locked-1605 dense 4096 as 31886, 4.9% above this 30401 recorded two days later at the same lock. This entry keeps 30401 because it is the number with sample-level provenance (7 samples, per-sample clock/power/throttle retained in grid_sweep_results.rds) and because it is the conservative choice — a future locked run reading 31886 scores 105% (improvement), not a regression. Gated only when bench_regress.R is run with --clock-locked 1605; SKIPPED otherwise.

4096_4096_4096.note: Power-bound kernel: it draws >150 W mid-run, so at native boost a varying fraction of the bench's 50 averaged launches hits SwPowerCap, giving a ~1.9x bimodal average with no fair baseline. Measured under a host-side clock lock (Windows nvidia-smi.exe -lgc 1605,1605, elevated): median of 11 valid samples, 2026-05-22, spread 1.02x (within ±5%). 1605 MHz is the highest clock the lock holds cleanly — above it the kernel sags back under the 150 W cap (clock_lock_sweep.R: 1605->50.5k, 1710->50.9k, 1785->SwPowerCap). Gated only when bench_regress.R is run with --clock-locked 1605; SKIPPED otherwise (the pre-push hook does not lock, by design). Supersedes the removed 2026-05-10 power-fault entry (4.449 ms / 30889). See docs/inventory.md and issue #131.

1024_8_8.note: median of 5 valid samples, 2026-05-10. +17% throughput vs 2026-05-05 baseline (was 2.810 / 6112) — real improvement from regpv tuning between recordings. Wider tolerance (0.30): this TC-compute-bound kernel is strongly SM-clock-sensitive, and a short single-process bench_regress run cannot drive the laptop GPU to the 1785 MHz boost bin — it caps at 1410 MHz (measured 2026-05-21: 8-run spread 5394-5651 GFLOPS, min/baseline 0.754, exactly the 1410/1785 clock ratio of the 7152 boost-clock baseline; power 43 W, 50 °C, no throttle). Not a code regression. Tolerance matches the igemm_sparse_tiled 4096³ entry (same laptop-artifact pattern). Re-investigate / narrow once clock-locking lands (#125).
